sentences.text: Elbretornis was an extinct genus of enantiornithine birds that lived in what is now Salta Province, Argentina, during the late Cretaceous period.
The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — indicates the animal was 33 cm long, had a hip height of 24 cm, and weighed 570 g.
Besides the holotype, fossils of other specimens include dorsal vertebrae, a sacrum, a femur, a rib, and a tibiotarsus.
Like other enantiornithines, Elbretornis bones were highly pneumatized, implying an adaptation for flight.
The genus Elbretornis and its only known species, Elbretornis bonapartei, were named by Cyril A. Walker and Gareth J. Dyke in 2009.
Elbretornis bonapartei lived approximately 70 million years ago.
Elbretornis lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.

Researchers debate whether Elbretornis is a distinct genus or if it actually belongs to previously described genera like Lectavis, Soroavisaurus, or Yungavolucris due to the scarcity of known fossil elements.
